_meta.note: Hand-authored expectations for the posture rule sanity audit (audit_posture.py). Read by that script only: nothing at runtime and nothing in the build reads this file. It is a SANITY CHECK on rules that were written from the literature, not a training set and not a labelled corpus -- every clip here was chosen because a human can say what the body is doing in it without measuring anything, and the expectations are written at that level (a set of acceptable answers, not one).

expectation_keys.dominant: dominant_posture must be one of these
expectation_keys.start: start_posture must be one of these
expectation_keys.end: end_posture must be one of these
expectation_keys.contains: each of these postures must appear in at least one segment
expectation_keys.never: none of these postures may appear in any segment
expectation_keys.boundaries: exactly `count` posture_transitions between the two states in `between`, counted in either direction

_meta.always_checked: No posture segment may be shorter than min_frames = round(MIN_POSTURE_DURATION_S * frame_rate), unless it is the clip's only segment -- a two-frame Mixamo pose has no longer segment available.
_meta.version_note: 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0 added `root_travel` and changed no posture rule. 1.1.0 -> 2.0.0 replaced the seated rule with a mechanical one: Winter (1995) on the centre of mass over the base of support, Hof et al. (2005) for the extrapolated COM that makes it hold for a body in motion, de Leva (1996) for the COM itself. The ten cases added below are what motivated it -- nine deep stances that read `seated` at 1.1.0, and the straddled chair, which reads `other` and is recorded as an ACCEPTED answer rather than a miss. The three transition cases now allow their crossing to pass through `other`: that is Schenkman's momentum-transfer phase, and it is one crossing spent over two boundary events.

cases.why: an idle stand: nothing but standing
still an idle stand; the head turning must not move the posture
a two-frame Mixamo pose of a walk, upright throughout
a walk cycle: the swing leg must not read as anything but standing
seated for the whole clip
starts on the feet and ends seated; only the END is asserted here

the canonical sit-down: standing to seated, once. The crossing may be direct or may pass through `other` -- Schenkman's momentum-transfer phase, where she has left her feet and the seat is not carrying her yet -- and either is one crossing
the canonical stand-up, and unidirectional: seated to standing, once, nothing after. A second seated run after the rise would be a second crossing and would fail this count
rises out of a seat to celebrate AND SITS BACK DOWN. Two crossings is the right answer here, and asserting one would be asserting that the clip is something it is not
begins face down on the ground; only the START is asserted here
on hands and knees the whole way
prone the whole way
crouched behind cover throughout; a crouch is not a sit
starts crouched and ends upright, so only the start is asserted
kneeling throughout; a kneel is not a sit
kneeling and reaching down; still not a sit
bent forward over the knees but standing on them; bending is not lying down
a low hop, peaking at h_body 1.133 against H_AIRBORNE 1.15: it stays an upright state, and must never read as seated or floor
a running jump, peaking at h_body 1.475: the airborne frames must not read as standing
upright, then down: must end on the floor
upright, then down: must end on the floor

cases.category: deep stance / squat: must not end seated
cases.why: the bottom of a swing: hinged at the hips, loading a lift rather than sitting on anything

cases.category: deep stance / squat: must not end seated
cases.why: braced to pull, weight forward over the feet, which is the opposite of a seat

cases.category: deep stance / squat: must not end seated

cases.category: deep stance / squat: must not end seated
cases.why: ends folded down with the feet under the body and the COM 0.15 m in front of the heels. It passed every angle the 1.1.0 rule asked for and is the clip that made the case for a mechanical test rather than a tighter one

cases.category: straddling a seat: the feet carry the body
cases.why: sitting BACKWARDS on a chair, astride it, feet planted either side. Reads other at 2.0.0 and that is the definition working: the COM is 0.023 m in FRONT of the heels, so the feet are carrying the body and nothing about the balance says seat. An accepted case, recorded here so the answer is a decision rather than a surprise
